name: Container ship
headline: length
subtitle: Ever Alot, an Evergreen A-class ship of 24,004 TEU
description: The biggest container ships are about 400 m long and carry more than 24,000 standard 20-foot containers. Ever Alot, built by China's Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding for Evergreen Marine and delivered in June 2022, measures 399.99 m long and 61.5 m wide. It was the first ship able to carry more than 24,000 TEU, and Guinness World Records lists it among the record holders for container capacity.

facts.text: Ever Alot can carry 24,004 TEU (twenty-foot equivalent units), 12 TEU more than its predecessor Ever Ace.
Ever Alot was the seventh ship in Evergreen's series of 13 A-class ships and the first in the world over 24,000 TEU; it is classed by ABS and was deployed on Far East to Europe routes.
Guinness World Records lists Ever Alot, Ever Atop and Ever Aria as the largest container ships by capacity, with a gross tonnage of 236,228.
According to Guinness, these ships stop just short of 400 m because ships over 400 m count as oversized and pay higher docking fees at many ports.

sources.title: World's Largest Containership Ever Alot Delivered in China

caveats: No page from Evergreen or Hudong-Zhonghua itself could be read; the 399.99 m length, 61.5 m width and 33.2 m depth are the builder's figures as reported by MarineLink at delivery.
Guinness World Records gives the length as 399.9 m (1,312 ft), slightly different from the 399.99 m reported at delivery.
Gross tonnage (236,228) is a measure of enclosed volume, not weight, so it is not stored as a mass. No source gave the ship's actual mass (lightship weight or displacement).
The record status quoted is as shown on the Guinness page in September 2026; newer ships may since have been reported with higher capacities.
